title: The Mystery Destination Walk
clue: Four envelopes sit on the fridge, and nobody has opened one yet.
reveal: You pre-check three dog-friendly places, seal each in an envelope and let them wait a day. Your dog's nose picks one, you open it at your own door and go. The core places are a short walk from home; a day trip by car is the optional upgrade.
objective: Walk to a destination drawn from sealed, pre-checked envelopes, with time to sniff and rest, then seal a new one for next time.
instructions: A day ahead, choose three places within about ten minutes' walk where dogs are welcome and you can pause: a bench by water, a quiet green corner, a bridge, a calm small square. Check each one: rules, shade, noise, and no booking needed. Write each on a card with a one-line plan, and add a fourth card, Plan B: the doorstep. Better still, let someone else in your home write the cards so the surprise is real for you.
Seal each card in an envelope, shuffle them and prop them on the fridge. Leave them unopened all day. The wait is part of it.

On the day, check the weather. If it is too hot, icy or stormy, the Plan B envelope is the one you open. Otherwise lay the envelopes on the floor and let your dog's nose choose: the first one they sniff or settle by is the one. If they show no interest, draw one yourself.
Open it at your front door and read it aloud. Walk there on a loose leash at your dog's pace.
At the destination, give your dog a sniff stop with no time limit, then a rest: sit, offer water and do nothing. Your dog's exit is always home; if they head that way, follow.
Give the place a rating in your own words, on any scale you like, such as three puddles and a lamppost.

At home, write a new card for a place you noticed on the way, seal it and prop it on the fridge, and file the opened envelope in a shoebox with a line about what you found. Nothing is due and there is no count; it is simply something waiting.
twist: The surprise is real for you and safe for your dog, because you vetted every envelope yourself, and your dog's nose picks which one opens.
variations: Day-trip version (needs a car): draw from three pre-checked destinations within a drive your dog handles (a woodland trail, a quirky roadside landmark, a quiet viewpoint), with a rest at each. Check dog and leash rules, shade, water, parking, hours and any booking. Restrain your dog in the car, take regular breaks and check the car's temperature before loading. Seniors: shorter drives, and ask your vet about travel comfort. If they seem travel-sick, make it a short local walk.

At-home or seated version: the envelopes hold Door, Middle and Home cards instead of places (a window seat, a slow lap of the room, a few lines read aloud while your dog settles), opened in turn, plus a Dog's Veto slip: 'If my dog would rather not, we stay in and sit together.'

Hint-card version: seal one hint the night before ('something yellow', 'somewhere that smells green') instead of a place, hang it on the door handle, open it at the door and let your dog lead a short stroll to see what fits. A match and no match both count.
Nervous dog or quiet only: all three places are quiet corners at off-peak times, or three different rooms at home with a new corner to sniff.
completion: You have opened an envelope, visited it with a sniff stop and a rest, and sealed one for next time, or Plan B was the whole outing.
photoIdea: The opened envelope at your destination, with your dog sniffing beside it.
memoryPrompt: Which envelope did your nose-picker choose, and what is waiting in the next one?
substitutes: No envelopes: fold paper in thirds and tape it shut

reservation.note: Core: on foot, nothing booked. The day-trip version needs a car; check each place for dog rules, hours, parking and booking before sealing it.

safety: Sidewalk too hot for the back of your hand is too hot for paws; head home if your dog pants hard or shivers.
Check each place allows dogs, keep a leash on, and politely decline strangers who want to pet or feed.
Restrain your dog in the car, never leave them in a parked one, and take breaks with water.
